name: Does your security controls set map to the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)?
conditionsText:
The mapping should cover the service's relevant controls against applicable CAF outcomes.
CAF is structured around four high-level areas:
1. Managing security risk
2. Protecting against cyber attack
3. Detecting cyber security events
4. Minimising the impact of cyber security incidents
requirementTitle: Does your security controls set map to the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)?
requirementDescription: Can you show how the security controls selected for your service relate to the security outcomes in the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) Cyber Assessment Framework?
why:
The CAF provides a common, outcome-focused way of looking at cyber security and resilience.
The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) describes CAF as a systematic approach to assessing how cyber risks are being managed. Its high-level objectives and principles are expressed as security outcomes rather than a simple checklist of individual technical measures.
tasks: Does your security controls set map to the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)?

actions.title: Does your security controls set map to the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF)?
actions.description:
• Take the service's agreed security controls set.
• Map each relevant control to the corresponding CAF outcome/principle.
• Identify any CAF areas with insufficient control coverage.
• Address or explain gaps where appropriate.
• Maintain the mapping as the controls and service change.
